content:
Federal Deputy Carlos Canturosas Villarreal of Nuevo Laredo is backing a landmark reform approved unanimously by Mexico's Chamber of Deputies — 419 votes in favor — that makes criminal recruitment a standalone crime punishable by up to 25 years in prison, with special protections for children and adolescents, according to Luis Valtierra Noticias (Oct. 21, 2026).

The legal change closes gaps that had made it difficult to prosecute these offenses and allows authorities to intervene from the moment a person is lured into joining a criminal group. Recruitment methods, according to the bill's text, include deception, false job offers and contact through social media.

Under the reform, the basic form of the offense carries 10 to 20 years in prison. When committed through threats, coercion, violence or abuse of power, sentences rise to 15 to 25 years, plus additional aggravating factors.

One of the reform's central provisions: the recruitment of minors will be considered forced even when no explicit threats or violence can be demonstrated — recognizing the particular vulnerability of young people to criminal groups' recruitment strategies. Authorities will also be able to open investigations on their own initiative, without requiring a formal complaint from the victim.

Canturosas said confronting criminal recruitment requires legal tools that punish those responsible while protecting people's freedom, integrity and human dignity — particularly those in vulnerable conditions.

After its approval in San Lázaro, the bill was sent to the Senate, where the legislative process continues.

Sources: Luis Valtierra Noticias, "Carlos Canturosas respalda reforma contra el reclutamiento criminal; contempla penas de hasta 25 años" (Oct. 21, 2026).

excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's federal deputy Carlos Canturosas backed the Chamber of Deputies' unanimous 419-vote reform making criminal recruitment a standalone crime with up to 25 years in prison — including forced recruitment of minors. The bill now heads to the Senate.
title: Canturosas backs reform making criminal recruitment a crime carrying up to 25 years; bill heads to Senate
